issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode silently changed from EXTERNAL to FIXED — breaking behavior change for existing users
issues.detail: The default for `turn_detection_mode` flipped from `EXTERNAL` to `FIXED` (line ~208 in stt.py). Existing users on `0.0.99` who relied on the documented default will get a different endpointing pipeline (Pipecat-controlled, with VAD frame handling disabled inside the plugin). The changelog is filed under `3328.fixed.md` rather than `3328.changed.md` / `breaking.md`, and there is no deprecation notice. At minimum this needs an explicit BREAKING note and a migration line in the changelog. Consider whether bumping the default deserves a major-version note.

issues.description: Handler still keys off `_enable_vad` but the membership semantics changed — verify branch coverage
issues.detail: `_enable_vad` is now False for both `FIXED` and `EXTERNAL` (previously only `EXTERNAL`). The handler at the bottom of `process_frame` warns 'internal VAD is being used' when `_enable_vad` is True and a `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` arrives, and finalizes otherwise. Because `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` is, by name, a VAD-originated frame, in `ADAPTIVE`/`SMART_TURN` modes (where `_enable_vad` is True) it will only warn and not finalize — that may be intentional, but the inverted naming (`elif not self._enable_vad`) is hard to read and worth a comment or a positively-named flag (`_finalize_on_external_vad`). Confirm `FIXED` mode actually receives `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` upstream; if it does not, finalization will never trigger.

issues.description: Frame type switched from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame without documented rationale or back-compat path
issues.detail: `process_frame` previously finalized on `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame`; it now only finalizes on `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame`. Any pipeline that emits `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` without the VAD subclass (e.g. manual turn control, custom user-turn aggregators, tests, or processors that push the base class) will silently stop finalizing transcription. This is a behavior regression for non-VAD pipelines. Either keep the base-class check as a fallback, or document loudly in the changelog that `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` is now required upstream.

issues.description: `speech_segment_config` is unconditionally overwritten, clobbering any value set via the generic config-copy loop
issues.detail: `_prepare_config` first copies known attribute names from params onto `config`, then unconditionally assigns `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)`. If `speech_segment_config` ever becomes an InputParams field (or is inherited from a preset), this assignment will silently overwrite it. Either fold `split_sentences` into the copy loop, or guard the assignment (`if params.split_sentences is not None`).

issues.description: `params.split_sentences or False` collapses None and False — fine today, fragile tomorrow
issues.detail: `split_sentences: bool | None = None` is then coerced via `or False`. That works, but if the SDK ever distinguishes 'unset' from 'explicitly false' (e.g., to inherit a preset default), this coercion will hide the unset case. Prefer `emit_sentences=bool(params.split_sentences)` for intent, or pass through `None` if the SDK accepts it.

issues.description: Commented-out `start_processing_metrics()` call moved but not resolved
issues.detail: In `_handle_start_of_turn` the `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line was moved from below the two awaits to above them, but it is still commented out. If metrics belong here, uncomment them; if not, delete the line. Moving dead code without explanation is a code-review smell and makes future archaeology harder.

issues.description: Two changelog files for one PR — `added` and `fixed` overlap and the `added` entry is mis-categorized
issues.detail: `3328.added.md` documents `split_sentences` (genuinely added) while `3328.fixed.md` documents the VAD frame switch, the default change, and the emit-gating. The default-change item is a behavior change, not a fix, and arguably belongs under `changed`/`breaking`. Splitting one PR across multiple changelog buckets is fine; mis-bucketing breaking changes as fixes is not.

issues.description: Docstring for `turn_detection_mode` lists modes inconsistently — `EXTERNAL` description is now stale
issues.detail: The class-level `TurnDetectionMode` docstring still says 'If using Pipecat's built-in endpointing, then use TurnDetectionMode.FIXED (default)' but does not describe what `EXTERNAL` now means relative to `FIXED`. Users will need to know the difference (FIXED = Pipecat fires `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame`, EXTERNAL = caller drives finalization explicitly, or whatever the intended semantics are). Add a one-line description per enum value.

issues.description: No tests added for new `split_sentences` parameter or the new finalization path
issues.detail: The PR adds a user-facing parameter (`split_sentences`) and changes the frame type that triggers finalization, but no tests are included in the diff. At minimum a unit test verifying (a) `SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=...)` is set correctly from params and (b) `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` triggers `_client.finalize()` when `_enable_vad` is False would lock in the contract.

dissents.topic: Is the default flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED a P0 break or an acceptable P1?

positions.position: Changing a documented default is a breaking change. Without a major bump or explicit BREAKING note, existing integrations will silently behave differently — block merge until the changelog is reclassified and a migration note is added.
Speechmatics SDK 0.0.99 itself is pre-1.0; the plugin clearly tracks upstream. A loud changelog entry and release notes are sufficient. Treat as P1 — document and ship.

dissents.topic: Should the finalize fallback on `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` be preserved?

positions.position: Keep `isinstance(frame, (UserStoppedSpeakingFrame, VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame))` so pipelines that emit the base class still finalize. Lose nothing, gain robustness.
If `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` is now the canonical VAD signal in Pipecat, listening to both invites double-finalization and obscures the contract. Force callers to upgrade.

dissents.topic: Where does `split_sentences` belong — copy loop or explicit assignment?

positions.position: It is already in the `valid_params` list; let the copy loop set it on `config.speech_segment_config.emit_sentences` (or remove it from the list). Two code paths setting overlapping state is the bug magnet.

`SpeechSegmentConfig` is a structured sub-config; constructing it explicitly is clearer than relying on `setattr` walking nested attributes. Keep the explicit assignment, drop `split_sentences` from `valid_params`.

review.summary: The PR is a focused upgrade to the Speechmatics SDK 0.0.99 contract: a new `split_sentences` param, a new `FIXED` turn-detection mode that becomes the default, and a switch from `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` to `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame` as the finalization trigger. The core mechanics look correct, but three behavior changes (default flip, frame-type swap, VAD-enablement set membership) ship without back-compat shims and are filed under `fixed` rather than `changed`/`breaking`. No tests accompany the new param or the new finalization path, and one unconditional assignment of `speech_segment_config` could clobber future structured config. Recommend P1 fixes — reclassify the changelog, add a back-compat or migration note for the frame switch, guard the `speech_segment_config` assignment, and add a smoke test — before merge.
